answer: Reputation Prism Split. Each agent identity carries a reputation balance that splits across every identity sharing its underlying hardware or network vertex, so a new clone starts with a fraction of the parent's score and must independently earn the remainder through work. Sybil operators pay the full cost of organic reputation-building per clone while sharing the same capped origin, making N identities cost roughly N times the earned-reputation effort.
